steps: Unpack & check the packet
Unbolt the insert from its pallet and bend up the shipping clips. Check the manual packet: the glass latch tool, remote, backup battery holder and power harness all stay with the homeowner.

Open the white manual-packet box; contact Mendota Technical Service if anything is missing.

Glass latch toolHA-77-00256
Remote transmitterHA-110-00105 · 3 AAA (65-06-01270)
Backup battery holder05-02-00345 · 4 AA (65-06-01147)
Backup power harness10-03-00128

These and the owner's manual must stay with the homeowner. Not included: surround, log set, firebox liner and decorative front, each chosen and bought separately.
Level the insert

Use the four leveling bolts (1/4" to 1" of adjustment) only if the floor is more than 1/4" out of level; shim smaller differences with sheet metal. Never remove the bolts or use them to raise the unit.

• Reach the bolts by removing the angled burners and the air box.
  • Leave them installed: removing them leaves holes that draw air into the firebox and hurt flame performance.
  • Never use them, or longer or aftermarket bolts, to lift the insert over an ash lip: that can cause oil-canning or expansion banging noises, which the warranty doesn't cover.
  • Raising it more than 1": reline the whole firebox floor with refractory brick (firebricks and mortar, or a metal box made for the purpose), not blocks under the four corners.
LP conversion (if burning LP)

Before the insert goes into the cavity, fit kit HA-142-00027: the motorized LP regulator, #63 orifices on both angled burners, #62 on the pan burner, and the pilot clip pushed in until "NAT" is hidden.

Qualified service agency only. Shut off the gas supply, then turn off the electrical supply. Work in a clean environment.
  1. Close the appliance service valve; remove the 3 screws holding the valve assembly to the valve plate and tilt it forward.
  2. With a Torx T20 (supplied) or slotted screwdriver, remove and discard the two regulator mounting screws, the regulator tower and the spring and diaphragm assembly (if fitted). Check the rubber gasket is in position.
  3. Fit the stepper-motor LP regulator with the supplied M4 x 0.7 screws, threaded by hand, then torque to 25 lb-in ± 5. Stripped valve threads: replace the valve. Put the identification label on the valve body where it's easily seen.
  4. Remove the left and right angled burners (4 screws each; marked "L" and "R") and the floor (3 rear screws). Fit #63 orifices to both angled burners and the #62 to the pan burner.
  5. Pilot (right side of the firebox): hold its base with large vice grips, loosen the hood 1/4 turn counter-clockwise with a 7/16" open-end wrench (don't remove it), push the NG/LP clip fully in so "NAT" isn't visible, and retighten.
  6. Connect gas, confirm inlet and outlet pressures, and light with the remote: the main burner must light immediately without lifting, and pilot flames must be at least 1" long and overlap the propagation ports on both burners.

Attach the kit's labels to the back of the listing label plate in the side air gap.
Prepare fireplace & chimney

Clean, inspect and repair the firebox, flue and chimney top; remove doors, screens and the old chimney cap, and lock the damper open or remove it. Bring gas to the insert's left rear and 120 V to its right side.

• Masonry or factory-built ZC wood-burning fireplaces only. Badly deteriorated or damaged firebox: stop; repairs need structural-engineer review and code-official approval.
  • Clean the cavity and chimney per CSIA (masonry swept at 1/8" of sooty buildup), and inspect and repair the flue, especially unlined flues, and the chimney top.
  • ZC units: refractory, doors, screen rails, mesh, grates and mechanically fastened smoke shelves, shields and baffles may be removed. Never cut the fireplace's sheet metal. No gas access hole? Drill one of 1.5" or less through the lower sides or bottom and plug it with non-combustible insulation once the line is in.
  • Verify mantel clearance and the 16" non-combustible hearth extension.
  • Mechanically attach the supplied marking (fireplace converted for a gas insert only) inside the firebox. In a ZC fireplace, the warning label goes on the firebox floor beside the left or right wall, with self-drilling sheet-metal screws (not supplied).
Drop liners & seal the cap

Cut both 3" liners to reach 12" above the hearth floor (10' to 50' run), lower them with a weighted rope, and clamp and screw them to the cap's starter collars. Seal the cap base plate permanently to the chimney top.

1. Measure from the top of the chimney (or existing flue liner) to 12" (300 mm) above the hearth floor, allowing for offsets; a dropped rope works. Cut the liners to that length and mark exhaust and intake.
  2. Inspect the liners; replace any with tears or punctures.
  3. Fix a sheet-metal strap loop and rope to the liner end. From the roof, drop the weighted rope and feed both liners in; the person below guides them through the smoke shelf and damper, wearing leather gloves and safety glasses.
  4. At the cap, push each liner over its 3" starter collar, compress it tight, clamp with a 3" hose clamp close to the flashing plate, and add sheet-metal screws in two spaced spots so the clamp can't slide off.
  5. Seal the base plate airtight and permanently: trim it (1" overlap on a flat top; 1-1/2" bigger all round on a terra cotta liner, notched and bent into screw flanges; 2" larger on a steel pipe), wire-brush the top, lay a 1/4" bead of exterior-grade silicone, and screw it down.

Full-size cap only, at least 3" below any chimney cap (6" under caps or slabs over 16" wide). Caps near each other need an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier 6" taller than the highest cap and 3" wider past their edges; two direct vent caps need 18" between centerlines. A wood-burning flue less than 36" away (centerlines): a metal divider plate is recommended, or extend that flue liner 24" above the gas cap's top.
Damper & vent adapter
Set the air-intake damper for the vent length (factory 45° below 20'), then clamp and screw the 3" exhaust and 3" intake flex to the unit's vent adapter.

Below 20'leave at the factory 45°
Above 20'close about 15° for every 10' above 20'

Offsets and other factors may call for fine-tuning. To take the adapter off the unit, hook the spring-loaded latch at the front with the glass latch tool, pull forward and lift. Connect each flex to its starter collar as at the cap: compress, hose clamp, and two sheet-metal screws so the clamp can't slide off. No silicone at flex joints.
Slide in, connect & leak-test
Slide the insert about 6" into the opening, make the final gas connection and leak-test every joint, then connect power. Loop the spare gas flex and cable, and latch the vent adapter.

1. Slide the insert about 6" into the fireplace opening.
  2. Gas: the factory 48" × 3/8" stainless flex (3/8" male NPT adapter) exits the back, or can be rerouted out the side at the ball valve, and leaves 32" loose outside the body. Make the final connection and leak-test all field and factory joints with soap solution or a gas sniffer; verify pressures, orifice sizes and input rate.
  3. Power: make the final connection (cord or MC cable) and verify it.
  4. Form large vertical loops of the spare gas flex and MC cable behind or beside the insert so it can be pulled out for service.
  5. Slide the vent adapter forward between its guide rails, its flat front section on the insert top, then pull it back into place with the spring-loaded lever and latch it to the front of the unit.
Surround & front
Hang the Basix or Faceplate surround on the shoulder rivets at the insert's front edges, then mount the decorative front or door kit and the barrier screen.

Faceplate surrounds are only for Mendota door kits (Andover, Bentley, Prairie, Homestead, Willow); Basix surrounds take every other decorative front and screen-only installs. Stock sizes (H × W): small 24" × 36", medium 27" × 40", large 31" × 44", each with a flat, 1/2" or 1-3/4" outer edge; custom shapes and edges are available.

  1. Unwrap and inspect the surround; report damage to your Mendota dealer.
  2. Slide its inner flanges inside the insert's outer edges, line the hooks up with the factory shoulder rivets on both sides, lift slightly and hook on.
  3. The four #8 × 1/2" screws supplied are optional, and Mendota discourages using them. Level and plumb the insert so it can't tip forward and push the hooks off the rivets.
  4. Mount the chosen decorative front or door kit and the glass barrier screen.
Liner, logs & air shutters
Install the firebox liner kit and the White Oak or Birch log set per their own instructions, then set the burner air shutters for the fuel and fine-tune the flame.

Logs and coals must not block the pilot or main burner flames. Give the log set instructions to the homeowner.

Natural gasleft 1/8" · right 1/8" · floor 1/4" open
Propaneleft 1/2" · right 1/4" · floor fully open

Then adjust each tube for final flame appearance: too blue, close in small 1/8" steps until a realistic yellow; soot on logs or glass, open until it burns clean. Try each setting about 1/2 hr before changing again; very small changes make major differences. Above 4,500' some variation may be needed.
Test fire, cure & hand over
Confirm the pilot lights both burners at once and the flame is stable after 5 minutes, run the 3-step curing cycle, train the owner and register the warranty.

Before final operation

  • Glass gasket seal checked (corner joints butt together) and the glass frame properly latched.
  • Pilot lights immediately and lights both front and rear burners; flames travel promptly along each burner.
  • Burner cycles on/off without delay; flame stable and not lifting after 5 minutes. After a lockout, wait at least five minutes before relighting.

Curing

Run the 3-step curing cycle as the final install step, before finishing materials go on: Manual (OFF), flame Hi, fan level 3 for at least 2 hours, then cool; Hi with the fan off until odors diminish; then fan level 1. Expect smoke and odor; ventilate and allow for smoke alarms.

Hand-over

Train the owner on the remote (IPI/CPI, flame, fan, accent light, rear burner, the three thermostat modes), lockout reset, the backup battery pack, the master switch and the manual gas valve, glass door and front removal, the barrier screen requirement and periodic maintenance. Leave the manual packet, complete the final checklist and register the warranty at mendotahearth.com/warranty.

panels.title: Soot on glass or logs
items: Incorrect gas pressure or orifice size: outlet 3.5" W.C. NG / 10" W.C. LP
Leaking glass gasket: bulging corners, or white through the bulb along the top edge
Still sooting: open the burner air shutter; then shut off and call Mendota service

panels.title: Pilot slow to light / keeps sparking
items: Over ten seconds to light → check spark rod position and igniter wires for pinched or damaged areas
Sparking continues more than five seconds after the pilot lights → dirty flame sensor; clean with emery cloth
Still sparking → check the flame sensor lead wire for damage or grounding problems

panels.title: Delayed ignition or lifting flame
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or main burner flame
Pilot flame not reaching the burner: needs 1" minimum, overlapping the propagation ports
Slow flame propagation → remove debris and vacuum the burner ports
Under-firing (orifices or pressure below nameplate) can cause delayed ignition

panels.title: Lockout
items: Pilot fails to light → system locks out; wait at least five minutes before relighting
Frequent lockout → diagnose the primary cause; never assume the ignition control is faulty
Cold flue in winter → CPI raises startup draft and helps prevent lockout

light.title: Turning it on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace lights its own pilot with an electronic igniter. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Before you start

  • Sniff all around the fireplace for gas, including down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.
  • If you smell gas, don't light any appliance. Follow the steps in Gas smell & safety.
  • Make sure the master switch is on. It's at the bottom right corner, in the side air gap.

Light it

  1. Press On/Off on the remote. You'll hear a beep, then the igniter starts sparking.
  2. Once the pilot is lit and steady, the gas valve opens and the burner lights at full flame.
  3. Turn the flame down to a level you like with the remote.

If the thermostat icon shows ON or SMART, it only lights when your set temperature is above the room temperature. On OFF (manual) it lights and starts on Hi.

No flame? It may be in lockout (see Won't light? Reset lockout). To turn it off, press On/Off again.

Note: p. 68 says that with the master switch off only the main burners are disabled and everything else, including the continuous pilot, still works; p. 73 says the remote won't communicate unless the master switch is on.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote comes pre-programmed to your fireplace and takes 3 AAA batteries. Keep it within 20' of the fireplace. Each button press gives one beep. No beep? Press again.

The four buttons

  • On/Off: lights or shuts off the fireplace.
  • Thermostat: OFF (manual, runs whatever the room temperature), ON (turns itself on and off, running until the room is 1°F above your setting) or SMART (holds your setting by turning the flame up and down itself).
  • Mode: picks flame height, fan, accent light or rear burner.
  • Up/Down: changes that setting, or the set temperature.

Flame height and accent light have six levels each; the fan has six speeds plus off. Down at flame level one turns the burners off. For less heat, turn off the rear burner or lower the flame; a slower fan spreads less of it. On ON or SMART, the fan starts five minutes after the fireplace does and runs 12-1/2 minutes after the flames go out.

The checklist on p. 86 says the fan runs 12 minutes after the flames go out; pp. 21 and 69 say 12-1/2 minutes.

It shuts itself off after 24 hours on manual, or on ON or SMART if it hears nothing from the remote for 60 minutes (remote in another room, or very weak batteries).

Child lock: press Mode and Up together; again to unlock. °F/°C: with the fireplace off, press Mode and Thermostat together. Re-pair: with the master switch on, press the sync button above it (three beeps), then On within seven seconds (four beeps).

curing.title: First fires: smoke and smell
curing.html:
The first fires burn off materials left from manufacturing and harden the paint, so visible smoke and a strong smell are normal. Your installer is meant to run this curing cycle as the last step of the install, before finishing materials go around the fireplace:

  1. Step 1: with the barrier screen and any front fitted, set the thermostat to OFF (manual), flame on Hi, fan on level 3. Run at least 2 hours, then turn it off and let it cool.
  2. Step 2: same, but with the fan off. Run until the curing smell fades, and leave it on.
  3. Step 3: set the fan to level 1. If new curing smells appear, keep running until they fade.
Open doors and windows. The smoke will set off smoke alarms, so you may want to disable them for Step 1. Running the fan in Step 1 keeps the smoke from staining the wall above.

More than 10 hours on high isn't unusual. Slight odors may come back on later startups and fade with use.

Other smells

  • After three months or more unused: burnt dust and lint, like your furnace in the fall.
  • An old fireplace and chimney that weren't cleaned: the heat can make dirt, creosote or mold smell.
  • Adhesives, paints and wall finishes used wrongly around the fireplace can smell too.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass now and then, and only once it has cooled to room temperature.

  • Outside: any glass cleaner you like.
  • Inside: Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a comparable product. Take the glass door off first.
  • Never use oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners.
White film? The additives that make gas smell can harm the glass and leave a white film. It comes off if you clean it promptly.

Taking the door off

  1. Use the glass latch tool on the two spring latches on top: put the tip in the latch hole, pull toward you and turn 90° to release. Leave the hooks upside-down; it makes refitting easier.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the frame out about 8", lift it 1" at an angle, and set it aside.
  3. To refit, set the two bottom tabs in their slots, center the frame, tip it in until the gasket touches, and re-hook both latches with the tool, hooks facing down.
Check the gasket every time the door comes off. Never run the fireplace with the glass off, cracked or broken, and don't strike the glass or slam the door. Glass replacement is a job for a qualified person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI and CPI
modes.html:
An electronic igniter lights the pilot, and the pilot lights the main burners. You choose whether the pilot stays on between fires:

IPIpilot lights only when you call for heat, and goes out with the burners
CPIpilot stays lit; it shuts off after 7 days without use, and each use restarts the 7-day clock

To switch

With the remote off, press Mode. The screen shows CPI or IPI. Press Up for CPI or Down for IPI, then press On/Off to start the fireplace. A snowflake icon stays on the display in CPI.

In IPI, pressing Down at flame level one puts the pilot out too; in CPI the pilot stays on.

Why CPI in cold weather

A lit pilot keeps the chimney warm so it drafts well at ignition, eliminates excessive condensation on the glass, stops cold drafts and heat loss through the glass, and helps prevent lockouts.

Note: p. 2 says CPI is required in winter when outside daily highs stay at 50°F or lower; p. 72 says Mendota recommends CPI in winter when the average daily high falls below 50°F.

power.title: Power outages and batteries
power.html:
The fireplace normally runs on house power. In an outage it can run on the backup battery pack that came with it:

  1. Plug the battery pack's harness into the backup power inlet on the right side.
  2. Put four fresh AA batteries in the pack. They run the fireplace for about ten days.

On battery power the burner and flame height work, but the fan and accent light don't. The pack is 6V DC; never connect a higher- or lower-voltage source. Keep the pack and harness somewhere safe between outages. Your installer should show you how they work.

Note: p. 41 puts the backup power inlet directly below the master switch; p. 43 puts it above the sync button and master switch. Both put it on the right side.

Remote batteries

The remote takes 3 AAA batteries. A battery icon appears on its screen before they run out and goes away when you replace them. Very weak batteries can make the fireplace shut itself off on ON or SMART.

Thermostat icon gone after a battery change? Take one battery out, hold the Thermostat button while you put it back, and look for "set" (enabled) or "clear" (disabled). Repeat until you see the one you want.

lockout.title: Won't light? Resetting lockout
lockout.html:
If the pilot doesn't light, the ignition system shuts down for safety. This is called lockout. If the fireplace ignores the remote, it may be in lockout too.

Quick reset

Press On/Off to turn the system off; that resets the lockout. Wait five minutes for any gas in the unit to clear, then press On/Off to try again.

Full reset

If the remote works but the fireplace still won't turn on:

  1. Turn the remote off.
  2. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  3. Turn it off and wait two seconds.
  4. Turn it on and wait two seconds.
  5. Turn it off.

Wait at least five minutes, then turn the remote on and start the fireplace. Check that the master switch is on.

In cold weather, CPI pilot mode keeps the flue warm and helps prevent lockouts. See Pilot modes.
Still won't run? Turn off the gas (see Gas smell & safety) and call your Mendota dealer, service technician or gas supplier. If lockout keeps happening, have your dealer diagnose it. Don't assume the ignition control is faulty.

safety.title: Gas smell, shutting down and hot surfaces
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch or use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone, and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Shutting it down

In an emergency, flip the master switch off to stop the main burners. To turn off the gas: press On/Off, turn off CPI pilot mode, close the manual gas valve in the left-side convection chamber (glass latch tool, counter-clockwise 90°), close any outside shut-off valve, and cut the power before any service.

Every day

  • The barrier screen must be on whenever the fireplace runs. Replace a damaged one with Mendota's barrier for this model.
  • Keep furniture and any other objects at least 60" in front of the barrier screen, and nothing on the front edge of the mantel.
  • The glass and the surfaces around it get too hot to touch. That's normal, but watch children and pets closely. Running the fan cools the surroundings.
  • Never burn wood, paper or anything else in it. Keep clothing, gasoline and other flammables away.
  • Don't leave it burning unattended for long periods on manual.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Mendota requires replacing the whole appliance.

service.title: Yearly service and checks
service.html:
Have a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier service the fireplace every year, ideally in summer or early fall. Only they should adjust the burner, pilot or logs.

The yearly service

  • Clean lint and dust around the controls and blowers; check wiring under the burner.
  • Clean the flame sensor and sparker rods; vacuum the pilot assembly and burner ports.
  • Take out the logs and coals, clean the burner and logs, and check the logs for carbon.
  • Check the pilot and burner flames and the glass gasket seal.
  • Clear the vent cap of leaves, twigs and debris, and clean the glass.

What you can watch for

  • Check the outside vent cap monthly for anything blocking it.
  • At full flame, after 30 minutes or more, the rear flame normally reaches 1 to 2 inches above the top of the rear log.
  • Carbon on the logs: turn it off and call a qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier.
  • Soot patches bigger than 1" x 1" on the logs, a black film on the glass, or soot around the vent cap: turn it off and tell your Mendota dealer right away.

Lint from carpets and bedding can mean cleaning more often. The manual also lists "changing remote control at least every 6 months" as required, or more often with heavy use.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota's limited lifetime warranty covers the original purchaser while the fireplace stays where it was first installed. It can't be transferred. It starts on the date Mendota invoices your installing dealer, and only covers new units sold by an authorized Mendota dealer.

Which parts are covered, and for how long, is set out in a table on p. 87 of the PDF.

Making a claim

  • Report the problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, model name and serial number.
  • The serial number is on the listing label. Pull it out on its chain from the left-side air gap.
  • Your dealer submits the claim. If they can't, write to Mendota at the address in the manual.

What can void or limit it

  • Installation or repairs by an unqualified person, or no permits and inspections.
  • Skipped annual maintenance, which is the owner's job.
  • Over-firing, neglect, water damage, or a serial number removed or made illegible.
  • After three years from dealer purchase, Mendota may settle by paying the initial owner the unit's then-current wholesale price.
Discoloration, minor warping and small noises as the steel expands and contracts are normal. Clean plated trim only with denatured alcohol, and wipe off fingerprints before the first fire.

specInput.title: Input rates and efficiency
specInput.html:
NG high / low fire29,000 / 8,400 BTUH
LP high / low fire29,000 / 9,100 BTUH
P.4 efficiency78%

Natural gas input check: with orifices and manifold pressure verified and all other appliances and pilots off, run 30 minutes at maximum flame and read the meter before and after. (Final − initial, in therms) × 100,000 × 2 must be at least 29,000 Btu. For LP the manual checks orifice sizes and manifold pressure only.

Never over- or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or gas pressure; both void the warranty. Backyard natural-gas wells need gas analysis data sheets sent to Mendota before first firing. Above 7,500 ft, plan for input derating with the local gas company or Mendota Technical Service.

specInlet.title: Gas supply pressure and piping
specInlet.html:
Natural gas7" W.C. · 5.0" min / 11" max
Propane11" W.C. · 11" min / 13" max

Input and output pressure taps are on the main gas valve. Disconnect the appliance and its valve for supply-piping tests above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa); isolate it with its shut-off valve for tests at 1/2 psi or less.

Pipe size, supply regulator to the 48" flex adapter

Run (ft)Sch. 40 ID NG / LP · Type L OD NG / LP
0-101/2" / 3/8" · 1/2" / 3/8"
10-401/2" / 1/2" · 5/8" / 1/2"
40-1001/2" / 1/2" · 3/4" / 1/2"
100-1503/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 5/8"
150-2003/4" / 1/2" · 7/8" / 3/4"

Never plastic pipe. Drip leg recommended; brass-to-brass fittings on the flex line; leak-test with soap and water or a gas sniffer. A manual shut-off is factory-installed in the left-side convection chamber; add an external keyed valve where local code requires one.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure, pilot and flame
specManifold.html:
Natural gas3.5" WC ± 1/8"
Propane10.0" WC ± 1/8"

Check at the output pressure tap on the main gas valve. The soot chart's first check uses the same outlet pressures (3.5" W.C. NG; 10" W.C. LP).

Pilot and burner checks

  • Pilot flames at least 1" long, overlapping the flame sensor and the propagation ports on both rear and front burners.
  • Pilot lights within five to eight seconds of sparking; it rectifies and sparking stops within five seconds.
  • Burners light promptly and flame travels quickly and smoothly along their full length.
  • At maximum, after 30 minutes or more, a normal rear flame is 1 to 2 inches above the rear log's top edge (depends on gas type, air shutter and venting).

specOrifice.title: Orifices and LP conversion kit
specOrifice.html:
NG · pan burner#50
NG · angled (tube) burners L/R#52
LP · pan burner#62
LP · angled (tube) burners L/R#63

Sizes are stamped on the orifice body. The manual gives the same sizes for 0-2000 ft, above 2000 ft and 2000-4500 ft; see the data plate, and for high altitude consult the local gas distributor or authority having jurisdiction. When de-rating, fill in the High-Altitude De-Rating label from the manual packet and fix it to the back of the listing label plate.

LP kit HA-142-00027

One motorized LP pressure regulator (05-02-00346), two #63 orifices (65-14-00063) and one #62 (65-14-00062). The insert ships for natural gas; convert the regulator, pilot orifice slider and burner orifices before it goes into the cavity. Qualified service agency only.

specCavity.title: Minimum fireplace cavity
specCavity.html:
Minimum width29-5/8"
Minimum height19"
Min. depth · flat (5/16") edge17-5/8"
Min. depth · 1/2" edge17-3/8"
Min. depth · 1-3/4" edge15-7/8"

Masonry or factory-built ZC wood-burning fireplaces only. Width and height are fixed; the depth needed drops as the surround's outer edge gets deeper. Flat edges aren't available on arched surrounds.

To size the edge: set the floor cover plate (fully forward for a door-kit faceplate, fully rearward for a Basix; 1/4" of travel; never remove the plate), slide the insert in as far as it goes, and measure from the plate's front edge to the wall face the surround will butt against. Choose that depth or deeper; over 1-3/4" means a custom surround.

Net weight 160 lbs; team lifting recommended. The side lifting handles are for short moves only and can be removed once it's in place.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vertical termination only, through one of the approved co-linear flexible systems. 3" × 3" liners and vent caps are required; Mendota recommends running both liners all the way to the cap.

Vent run10' minimum · 50' maximum
Horizontalno horizontal runs; offsets under 4' if angled at least 30-degrees vertically
Cap top to chimney cap3" min · 6" under caps or slabs over 16" wide
The installation checklist on p. 49 prints a 4" exhaust liner. The ratings (p. 17) and venting pages (p. 37 and p. 59) give a 3" exhaust and 3" air inlet, and the same checklist calls for two 3" liners.

No low-profile or shallow-profile caps (exhaust recirculation, ghosting flames). Mendota highly recommends its caps AA-11-05280 (square) and AA-11-05281 (round), 3" × 3" with built-in flashing; flex kit AA-11-05282 has two 3" × 35' liners and 4 hose clamps. Liners and caps from BDM, Duravent, ICC, Olympia and RLH are also approved.

Screws and hose clamps at all four flex joints; no silicone at flex joints. Never share a flue with another solid-fuel or gas appliance. If the flue is too small for both liners, the intake can be stubbed short, but that may cause venting problems.

specClear.title: Clearances and hearth
specClear.html:
Combustible side wall18" from the visible glass's side edge
8" combustible mantel12" above the heat outlet top · 30-1/8" from the insert's floor level
Insert floor level to top air gap18-1/8"
Hearth pad, insert on the floornon-combustible, R-1, 16" in front
Hearth pad, insert raised2" less depth per 1" raised · none required at 6" or more

Side walls, corbels and mantel legs must sit behind a 45-degree line from the glass side edges unless more than 18" away. NFPA 211 shielding cuts side clearance by 66% (20-gauge or heavier steel on 1" standoffs) or 50% (R-1 ceramic or mineral board).

Non-combustible mantels can go at any height above the top convection opening. A pre-existing combustible mantel must fall within the approved mantel profile chart (a diagram on p. 29), be moved, or be shielded with 20-gage metal over a 1" air space, which takes the 12" down to 6".

A raised insert still heats the floor in front up to 200 °F; with carpet, vinyl or laminate, raise it at least 12". Paper-faced drywall (including Type X) and WonderBoard are not non-combustible.

Note: the R-value of mineral fiber board (Micore 160, 300, SB) at 1/2" is listed as 1.27 – 1.47 on p. 31 and 1.2 – 1.4 on p. 33. Rescor 360 (1.11) and Fiberfrax Duraboard LD (1.10) match on both pages.

specElec.title: Electrical
specElec.html:
Supply120 VAC · minimum line voltage 110 VAC
Backup6V DC pack · four AA
Accent lightG9, 25W bulb · part 10-11-00020
Note: the rating information on p. 17 gives the current as 1.5 Amps; the AC power section on p. 41 gives 2 Amp.

The supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it; ground per local code, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. The junction box with strain relief is on the right side. Either run the factory cord to a room outlet (or an outlet in a metal box inside the cavity, fed with 14-2 MC cable), or hard-wire 14-2 MC cable to the junction box with a 24" service loop. Circuits can't be shared between floors; an upper-floor fireplace needs a dedicated circuit from the main panel.

Note: the p. 42 heading gives the power cord length as 8-foot and the parts list gives 96" (p. 80); the p. 42 text and figure call it a 10' extension cord.
Note: p. 53 calls accent bulb 10-11-00020 a halogen G9 25Watt bulb; the parts list on p. 80 calls it a G9 Xenon, 25W bulb.

conflicts.issue: Master switch: p. 68 says that with it off only the main burners won't turn on and all other functions, including CPI, still operate; p. 73 says the remote won't communicate with the receiver unless the master switch is ON.

Winter CPI: p. 2 says it is required when outside daily highs remain 50°F or lower; p. 72 says Mendota recommends it when the average daily high falls below 50°F (the p. 86 checklist says 'suggested during cold season').
Backup DC inlet location: 'directly below the master switch' (p. 41) vs 'above the remote sync button and master power switch' (p. 43).
Current draw: 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps in the ratings information (p. 17) vs 120 VAC, 2 Amp in AC Power Requirements (p. 41).
Power cord length: 'Option 1: 8-foot power cord' (p. 42) and 'Power Cord, 96"' in the parts list (p. 80) vs 'the preinstalled 10' extension cord' and the '10-foot Power Cord' figure label (p. 42).
Accent bulb 10-11-00020: 'halogen G9 25Watt' (p. 53) vs 'G9 Xenon, 25W' (parts list, p. 80).
Exhaust liner size: 3" exhaust & 3" air inlet (ratings p. 17, venting pp. 37 and 59, 3" x 3" caps and kits) vs 'Run both 4" exhaust and 3" air intake liners' in the installation checklist (p. 49).
conflicts.corrected_to: 3" exhaust & 3" air inlet, as printed in the ratings (p. 17: "3" X 3" Liners & Vent Caps required"), the venting pages (pp. 37, 59) and the p. 49 checklist's own "two 3" liners" item

conflicts.issue: Mineral Fiber Board (Micore 160, 300, SB), 1/2": R-value 1.27 – 1.47 in the hearth pad board table (p. 31) vs 1.2 – 1.4 in the finishing materials table (p. 33).

Fan run-on after the flames turn off: '12-1/2 minutes' in the blower operation note (p. 21) and the normal thermostat mode description (p. 69) vs 'Fan delayed 5 minutes in ON and runs 12 minutes after.' in the final installation and homeowner checklist (p. 86).
conflicts.corrected_to: 12-1/2 minutes, as printed in the blower operation note (p. 21) and the normal thermostat mode description (p. 69)

conflicts.issue: Full lockout reset: the p. 77 sequence ends 'This should clear the lockout mode. Turn on the remote and start the fireplace.' with no wait; pp. 11, 66, 73 and 79 say to wait five minutes after a lockout before relighting (p. 11: 'always wait 5 minutes'; pp. 66 and 79: 'a minimum of five minutes').
conflicts.reason: Both fit: the five-minute wait on pp. 11, 66, 73 and 79 covers every lockout, so the guide's full reset now ends with it before the restart that p. 77 describes.

conflicts.issue: 8" combustible mantel height: the p. 29 text gives '12" above the top of the heat outlet (30.125" up from the floor level of this Insert)'; the figure caption shortens it to 'Minimum Distance from Floor to 8" Mantel is 30-1/8"'.
conflicts.reason: Same measurement: the caption's 'Floor' is the insert's floor level, as the p. 29 text and its note on the distance from the floor level of this Insert to the top air gap (18-1/8") show. The spec card row now reads 'Insert floor to 8" mantel', matching the specClear drawer.

review.notes: Catalog BTU (NG 29,000/8,400, LP 29,000/9,100) and 78% efficiency match p. 17 (manual says 'P.4', catalog basis 'P.4.1'). Catalog height/width/depth (19 / 29.625 / 17.625) equal the manual's MINIMUM FIREPLACE CAVITY (pp. 17, 22), not the insert's own size; the overall dimensions exist only as a drawing (p. 19), so they can't be checked. Catalog view area (28 3/4 x 18 1/8) and the 5-1/2" taper aren't in the manual text. Shown only as figures/tables, not transcribed: overall dimensions (p. 19), features and switch locations diagram (p. 20), approved mantel profile chart (p. 29, referenced in specClear), remote icons (p. 70), PF2 wiring diagram (p. 44), parts diagrams (pp. 81-83) and the warranty coverage table (p. 87; the warranty drawer points to it instead of giving periods). P. 16 has no text beyond its footer and p. 91 is blank. No LED/blink code table in the manual (only beeps), so codes is []. Fault panels come from the soot troubleshooting chart (p. 76), periodic inspection checks (p. 78), burner ignition characteristics (p. 57), over/under-firing (p. 79) and lockout guidance (pp. 2, 73, 79). Minor discrepancies not flagged in drawers: p. 72 calls CPI 'Pilot on Demand' while pp. 2 and 68 call it Continuous Pilot Mode (guide avoids the term); lockout reset is given two ways (p. 73: On/Off then wait five minutes; p. 77: off/on sequence), both shown; p. 62 text puts the cap-collar screws below the hose clamp while its figure caption says above, and says four #8 screws are needed with Mendota kits but eight for other brands (guide gives neither position nor count); the intake damper guide (p. 63) has an 'Above 50'' row although the maximum vent run is 50' (row omitted); the FAQ (p. 75) calls house power 110VAC while the electrical sections say 120 VAC; p. 2's 'Changing remote control at least every 6 months is required' is ambiguous (possibly the remote's batteries), so it is quoted, not interpreted. Hearth: the 2"-per-1" reduction and 'none required at 6" or more' are both given as printed (pp. 11, 31).
